core_obligations: Show that irreducibility over the separable closure implies geometric irreducibility: embed any extension k' into a field over the separable closure, use the preservation of irreducibility under passing to the separable closure and surjectivity of the projection to conclude that X_{k'} is irreducible (proof lines 1559-1566).

Assume reducibility over the separable closure and analyse an affine open covering: if a member is reducible over the closure or two members have empty intersection after base change, then X is reducible and one is done; otherwise one may assume all members meet after base change and that one affine member is reducible over the closure (proof lines 1569-1583).

Use the algebra lemma to find a finite separable extension k' over which that member is reducible, conclude that X_{k'} is reducible, and note that geometric irreducibility immediately implies the finite separable case (proof lines 1584-1592).
proof_roadmap: From reducibility of the closure to geometric irreducibility (proof lines 1559-1566).
Analyse an affine open covering to isolate one bad member (proof lines 1569-1583).
Descend reducibility to a finite separable extension (proof lines 1584-1592).
difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over a field k, the lemma shows the equivalence of geometric irreducibility, irreducibility of X_{k'} for every finite separable extension, and irreducibility of X over a separable algebraic closure (statement lines 1541-1556). The proof closes the three implications in a non-obvious order: assuming irreducibility over the separable closure, the author embeds an arbitrary extension k' into a larger field k-bar' over k-bar, uses that irreducibility is preserved by passing to the separable closure, and deduces irreducibility of X_{k'} by surjectivity of the projection, which gives geometric irreducibility (proof lines 1559-1566). For the converse direction the argument is more delicate: assuming X over the separable closure is reducible, the author exhibits an affine open covering and shows that if some member or some disjoint pair of members is already bad then X itself is reducible, so that one may assume the members meet after base change; then the algebra lemma on geometric irreducibility of finite type algebras produces a finite separable extension over which one member becomes reducible, hence X_{k'} is reducible (proof lines 1569-1588). The claim is H2: two standard inputs, but the reduction that forces a single affine member to be the culprit is a real step.
